idiom_name: diode: Circuit[Model] + ActionHandlers + Pot for async state (Scala.js)
implementation_notes: diode is the Scala library for managing an immutable application model - 'Circuit[M]' stores the model and owns action handling, ActionHandler/zoomTo define scoped pure reducers whose updated(...) returns a copy, composeHandlers combines them into one handler function, and the Circuit's subscription model notifies listeners when the model changes, with Pot modelling pending/ready/failed async states. What replaces the classic structure is the Circuit plus these handler classes; immutable case classes do the rest, since a handler returns a copy and never mutates the model. For server-side or reactive stacks the same one-way discipline is expressed as a fold over an action stream (Akka/Pekko typed, ZIO Ref plus queues) rather than a component store; the diode form is justified when a Scala.js UI shares state across many components.
pitfalls: A handler must return a copy (updated/copy), never mutate the model; vars or mutable collections inside the case class break the Circuit's change detection.
Effects belong outside the pure handlers (the Circuit's effect/async wrappers); performing I/O in handle breaks replay and makes ordering unpredictable.
Pot states (Pending/Ready/Failed) must be handled exhaustively in the view, or an async failure renders as stale content.
Subscribing a component without disposing the subscription leaks listeners for every mount; tie subscriptions to the component lifetime.
